title: Open Source Stewardship Communities: "We need you, but not your pull request"
abstract: arXiv:2609.12236v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human-centric AI for software engineering means keeping humans responsible for work performed with AI. In Open Source Software (OSS), AI lowers the cost of implementing changes, but reviewing someone else's contribution remains comparatively expensive, so some projects now restrict who may contribute implementations while still welcoming other participation---not because the code is AI-generated, but because it no longer justifies the review cost. We call the resulting form a stewardship community: a small core retains implementation authority while a broader community continues to shape the software without writing code, and access to coding increasingly depends on approval rather than self-initiated contribution. This raises a broader question: what happens to the human community when coding agents let maintainers replace implementation work once supplied by external contributors? For human-centric software engineering, keeping humans

translated_title: 开源管家型社区：“我们需要你，但不需要你的拉取请求”
translated_abstract: 面向人的软件工程AI意味着让人类对使用AI完成的工作负责。在开源软件（OSS）中，AI降低了实现代码变更的成本，但审查他人贡献的成本仍然相对高昂，因此一些项目现在开始限制谁可以贡献代码实现，同时仍然欢迎其他形式的参与——这并不是因为代码是AI生成的，而是因为代码贡献不再能证明其审查成本的合理性。我们将由此产生的社区形态称为“管家型社区”：一个小型核心团队保留代码实现的权威，而更广泛的社区继续在不编写代码的情况下参与塑造软件，且编写代码的准入越来越依赖于项目方的批准而非自主发起的贡献。这引出了一个更广泛的问题：当编码代理让维护者能够取代曾经由外部贡献者承担的实现工作时，人类社区将会发生什么变化？对于以人为中心的软件工程而言，保持人类的（此处摘要原文不完整）
tldr: 该论文提出“管家型社区”这一新概念，指出当AI大幅降低代码实现成本后，开源项目开始限制代码贡献、保留非代码参与，形成由小型核心团队掌握实现权、更广泛社区以不写代码的方式参与软件塑造的新形态。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the novel concept of "stewardship communities," revealing that as AI lowers implementation costs, open source projects increasingly restrict code contributions while welcoming non-coding participation, creating a new model where a small core retains implementation authority and the broader community shapes software without writing code.
